text: The value uses G(p+c), so an original degree-p element acquires degree p−c. Reindexing the direct sum by the bijection p↦p−c preserves its internal decomposition. This is the shift in [Stacks 00JL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL) and, for c=1, the suspension of [Keller §3.6](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bernhard.keller/publ/ioan.pdf#page=11). The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L76) passes.
Zero shift returns the original internal grading.
Evaluating the shifted piece gives the explicit p+c convention.

Each factor is spanned by its homogeneous elements, so their pure tensors generate the finite tensor product. Equality on these generators therefore gives equality of the linear maps. This applies the tensor universal property of [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL); the empty family still tests its unit tensor. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Coderivation.lean#L126) passes.
Actual application: homogeneous pure-tensor agreement uniquely determines the suspension Taylor map.

This transports every piece through [Mathlib’s opLinearEquiv](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Opposite.lean#L43), retaining its degree and the direct-sum decomposition. The definition concerns the module carrier; it does not introduce a multiplication or a Koszul sign. The op/unop membership controls check both directions of this transport. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Opposite.lean#L71) passes.
The image of an original homogeneous element has exactly the same degree.
Every opposite homogeneous element is detected by unop.

Unfolding shift gives exactly G(p+c). Thus the positive sign inside the index agrees with [Stacks 00JL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL); it lowers the degree of a fixed element by c. The zero-shift and iterated-shift equations check the boundary and composition conventions. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L76) passes.
At c=0 the original grading is recovered.
Two shifts evaluate to p+d+c, fixing the composition convention.

The value collects bidegree pieces with p+q=n. Each piece is generated by homogeneous pure tensors, and the existing internal bidegree decomposition proves their sum is direct. This is the total grading of [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL), extended here to commutative semirings; no flatness hypothesis is needed for split summands. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L148) passes.
A tensor of degrees p,q belongs to the piece p+q.
The whole degree-n piece is the sum over p and n−p.

The opposite piece is the image under [Mathlib’s opLinearEquiv](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Opposite.lean#L43). Applying its inverse unop proves precisely the displayed equivalence, for an arbitrary opposite element. No multiplicative structure on M or sign convention is assumed. The degree-zero inverse-map theorem checks this transport. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Opposite.lean#L91) passes.
The actual inverse linear equivalence preserves every homogeneous degree.

An original degree-p element has suspended degree p−1, so its sign changes from (−1)^p to (−1)^(p−1)=−(−1)^p. Homogeneous elements span, giving equality of linear maps. This follows the suspension convention in [Keller §3.6](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bernhard.keller/publ/ioan.pdf#page=11) and remains valid in characteristic two. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L88) passes.
The general parameter/shift identity specializes to the displayed negative sign.

For a degree-q map, the shifted input piece G(p+c) maps into H(p+c+q)=H((p+q)+c). Reindexing p proves the reverse implication too. This is simultaneous shift compatibility for the degree convention of [Stacks 00JL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL); the same shift on both sides is essential. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/AInfinity/Algebra/Transfer/Basic.lean#L96) passes.
Actual application: suspension retains degree +1 for the algebra differential.

On x⊗(y⊗z), the inverse associator returns (x⊗y)⊗z. The two total degrees p+(q+r) and (p+q)+r agree, and homogeneous generators span. Thus its stated degree is zero for the total grading of [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL); no permutation sign is introduced. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L188) passes.
The inverse linear equivalence also preserves total degree.

On a tensor of degrees p,r, the left sign is (−1)^(q(p+r)), while the right signs multiply to (−1)^(qp)(−1)^(qr). Bilinearity and homogeneous generation extend this equality to all tensors. This uses the total grading of [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL); both twist maps have degree zero. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L148) passes.
The input tensor has the total degree used in the sign computation.
At parameter zero the factors and total twist are identity maps.

The equation eliminates the condition p+q=n by substituting q=n−p. Submodule.map₂ is the span of bilinear images, and the supremum is their sum, so arbitrary finite sums are included. This is the degree-n piece described in [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL), without treating every tensor as pure. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L148) passes.
The p,q pure generator lands in degree p+q.
Containing the displayed generators implies containing the entire piece.

The generator x⊗y lies in the p-indexed image because (p+q)−p=q. This gives membership, even if the tensor vanishes; it makes no nonvanishing or unique-degree claim about zero. The formula is the homogeneous-generator rule in [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L167) passes.
Actual use on triple homogeneous tensors verifies compatibility with reassociation.

The ordinary TensorProduct.map sends x⊗y to f(x)⊗g(y). Their degrees become p+a and q+b, hence total degree increases by a+b. The proof uses homogeneous generators as in [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL). This is an unsigned map; the separate DG tensor convention adds an evaluation sign. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L204) passes.
Actual tensor map of degree-zero twists agrees with the total-grading twist.

The formula is the defining forward image under [Mathlib’s opLinearEquiv](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Opposite.lean#L43), not a preimage or a reversed degree. Since op is a linear equivalence, its image pieces retain both spanning and independence. The homogeneous membership equivalence checks that the carrier transport has the claimed meaning. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Opposite.lean#L71) passes.
Forward-image membership is equivalent to original piece membership.

An original degree-p vector has shifted degree p−c. Its sign is (−1)^(q(p−c))=(−1)^(qc)(−1)^(qp), since signs are self-inverse. Extending from homogeneous pieces gives the displayed scalar multiple. This uses [Keller §3.6](https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~bernhard.keller/publ/ioan.pdf#page=11)’s shift convention; all integer shifts and parameters are allowed. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L101) passes.
The c=q=1 specialization gives the suspended negative sign.

Every summand in the degree-n piece is generated by tensors from G(p) and H(n−p). A submodule containing these generators contains their span and their sum. This is the generator criterion associated with [Stacks 09LL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09LL); it does not claim all degree-n elements are pure tensors. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/TensorProduct.lean#L167) passes.
Actual application reduces reassociation to homogeneous pure generators.

Specializing inverse-image membership to op(x) cancels unop∘op. Thus the displayed equivalence preserves degree p in both directions. The only transport is [Mathlib’s opLinearEquiv](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Equiv/Opposite.lean#L43), so no multiplication, differential or Koszul-sign assertion is hidden in this lemma. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Opposite.lean#L85) passes.
The supplied forward linear equivalence is homogeneous of degree zero.

The left piece at p is G((p+d)+c), equal to G(p+(d+c)); grading extensionality gives equality of structures. Thus the written order d+c matches evaluation of the two reindexings. This is composition of the shifts of [Stacks 00JL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL), for arbitrary integers. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L76) passes.
Zero shift provides the identity boundary of this composition law.

At c=0 each piece is G(p+0)=G(p). Extensionality identifies the internal gradings, with proof fields irrelevant. This is the identity shift for [Stacks 00JL](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00JL), including the zero module and vanishing pieces. The [published control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Shift.lean#L71) passes.
Evaluating pieces gives the identity at c=0.

Small open balls are additive subgroups by the ultrametric inequality. The instance supplies exactly the [native NonarchimedeanRing field](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Nonarchimedean/Basic.lean#L45), retaining the seminorm topology. The normalized unit-ball specialization passes.
Under norm-one normalization, the closed unit ball is an open subring, a concrete open-additive-subgroup calibration.

The stored zero, negation and triangle laws build the intended operator seminorm. This is the seminormed extension of [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8); it does not silently assert Hausdorffness. Field-structure agreement and the zero-operator checks pass.
The entire scoped seminormed group structure agrees with Mathlib over nontrivially normed fields.
Zero operators, including zero-module cases, have norm zero.

Apply the target triangle inequality pointwise and then take the least uniform bound. This yields the norm law of [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8) under the displayed Tate assumptions. The published ultrametric maximum bound passes as a sharper specialization.
For an ultrametric target, the stronger maximum triangle inequality holds.

The admissible bound sets are literally equal after applying norm_neg, so this remains valid even for unbounded maps. On bounded maps it is the usual norm symmetry in [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8). The zero-map boundary passes.
Zero operators, including zero-module cases, have norm zero.

Evaluate exact scaling at1 and cancel the positive norm of a pseudo-uniformizer. The conclusion is independent of the chosen witness. The underlying norm_one theorem passes, giving the normalization used in [JN Definition2.1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8).
A chosen multiplicative pseudo-uniformizer forces norm one.

Tate boundedness makes the infimum a genuine least bound, so evaluating its membership gives the claim. This is the uniform-bound property in [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8). The bound equivalence and multiplication calibration pass.
A nonnegative constant bounds the operator norm exactly when it bounds every value over Tate scalars.
Multiplication by a vector has its norm over a norm-one ring; E=R gives the roadmap multiplication calibration.

The exact scaling equation at1 gives r=r‖1‖ with r>0. Thus JN’s norm-one convention is recovered rather than silently assumed. Nontriviality and the reciprocal-inverse consequences pass ([JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8)).
A pseudo-uniformizer excludes the zero ring.
The pseudo-uniformizer inverse has reciprocal norm.

Evaluate the scaling law at1 and cancel ‖u‖. This verifies the normalization implicit in [Martin’s multiplicative-unit argument](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32152?nt=1#page=15) under substantially weaker algebraic hypotheses. The published nontrivial normed-ring specialization passes.
The general norm-one identity specializes to multiplicative units in nontrivial normed rings.

Rescaling puts a nonzero-seminorm vector into the ball, with inverse factor at most ‖x‖/r^(k+1). The separate zero-seminorm argument is necessary and present. This quantifies the scaling behind [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8); the corresponding operator-norm estimate passes.
The same quantitative shell constant bounds the operator norm of a continuous linear map.

Starting from the shell (r,1], shift its unique exponent by k. Its upper endpoint puts the scaled norm below δ, while its lower endpoint yields the inverse-factor estimate. This makes the rescaling in [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8) quantitative; the local-to-global consequence passes.
The rescaling estimate gives the published local-to-global bound, including seminorm-zero vectors.

Exact action scaling extends in both directions along the unit powers. This is the power form of [JN’s multiplicative-unit module observation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8). The ring-power and inverse-action specializations pass.
The module power-scaling formula specializes to the ring itself.
Exponent minus one gives reciprocal scalar scaling on modules.

The function n↦r^n‖m‖ is strictly decreasing and crosses exactly one half-open shell. The endpoint convention avoids a double count when ‖m‖ is a power of r. This is the shell argument behind [JN §2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8); the quantitative ball-rescaling consequence passes.
The unique shell gives entry into a prescribed ball with inverse scaling controlled.

Forward induction uses exact unit scaling and backward induction uses reciprocal inverse scaling. No smallness assumption is needed. This extends [JN’s module observation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8) to integer powers; both ring-power specializations pass.
Integer-power module scaling specializes to powers of the unit in the ring.
The nonnegative-exponent specialization agrees with natural powers.

Apply exact u-scaling to u⁻¹•m and cancel the positive factor. The reciprocal convention is the same as [Martin Lemma1.21](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32152?nt=1#page=15); the pseudo-uniformizer inverse-action specialization passes.
Exponent minus one gives reciprocal scalar scaling on modules.

The two contractive inequalities squeeze the result to equality because the inverse has reciprocal norm. This is exactly the module observation following [JN Definition2.1.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1604.07739#page=8), with weaker action hypotheses. The pseudo-uniformizer specialization passes.
The unit module-scaling formula specializes to pseudo-uniformizers.

The forward implication of [Martin Lemma1.21](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32152?nt=1#page=15) needs only the scaling equations and a nonzero factor. The Lean statement correctly removes unused addition and norm-inequality assumptions. The norm-one ring characterization and pseudo-uniformizer specialization pass.
In a norm-one seminormed ring the reciprocal-inverse condition characterizes multiplicative units.
The pseudo-uniformizer inverse has reciprocal norm.

The carrier is f⁻¹(I), constructed as ker(q∘f) for q:K→K/I. Both maps are surjective, so [Stacks, tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9) supplies the coideal calculation without flatness. This extends the field convention in [Milne, Propositions 3.11–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). Published [augmentation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Augmentation.lean#L215) and [all-value-algebra points](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L247) controls pass; arbitrary nonsurjective maps are not claimed here.
Preimage of the counit kernel is the source augmentation ideal.
For every value algebra, precomposing a point matches membership in the pulled-back subgroup.

Forgetting the Hopf laws leaves [ordinary ideal preimage](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L47) exactly: the kernel of q∘f consists of x with f(x)∈I. The published [membership](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L100) and [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L189) controls pass. Surjectivity justifies the Hopf structure and does not replace the preimage by a generated ideal or saturation.
Element membership in preimage is exactly image membership.
Identity preimage recovers the original ideal.

Membership is tested by f(h)∈I, exactly as in [ordinary ideal preimage](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L47). The element on the left lies in H and its image on the right in K. The published [points-pullback comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Points/Basic.lean#L247) passes for every commutative value algebra and uses both directions of this formula. No preimage representative is chosen to define membership.
For every value algebra, precomposing a point matches membership in the pulled-back subgroup.

The composite has the correct order H→K→K/I, and vanishing in K/I is precisely membership in I. This is the quotient-kernel mechanism of [Milne, Propositions 3.11–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [carrier equality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L92) passes. Its displayed surjectivity proof composes the quotient map’s surjectivity with hf; no flatness or surjectivity of an unrelated map is inferred.
Underlying ideal is the ordinary preimage.

If f(h) lies in I⊆J, it lies in J; hence preimage preserves the ideal order, as in [ordinary ideal preimage](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L47). The published [binary-join control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L167) passes. The inequality concerns ideals in H and is not reversed by the contravariant geometric interpretation. Surjectivity remains present to construct the bundled preimages.
Surjective preimage preserves binary joins.

For k∈I, surjectivity supplies h with f(h)=k, so containment of preimages gives k∈J. This matches [Mathlib’s surjective order reflection](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L397). The published [two-direction control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L132) passes. The hypothesis is essential for detecting elements outside the image; the theorem does not assert order reflection for an arbitrary morphism.
Containment is both preserved and reflected.

Preimage both preserves and reflects containment under a surjective f, agreeing with [Mathlib’s surjective order reflection](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L397). The published [equality-reflection control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L140) passes by antisymmetry. Both I and J live in K; no identification of all ideals of H with ideals of K is claimed, since a preimage necessarily contains ker f.
Surjective preimage reflects equality of ideals.

Equality of preimages detects equality of codomain ideals because f is onto, as in [Mathlib’s comap injectivity](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L331). The published [image-after-preimage recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Map.lean#L303) passes and supplies an independent cancellation route. This is injectivity of the operation on ideals, not injectivity of f itself.
Image after preimage recovers codomain ideal.

The preimage of {0} is ker f, directly matching [ordinary ideal preimage](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L47) and [Milne, Propositions 3.11–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The published [quotient-kernel recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L282) passes, where this preimage is the original quotient ideal. Thus preimage need not preserve bottom as bottom; the statement correctly retains a potentially nonzero kernel.
The quotient map has exactly its defining ideal as Hopf kernel, without flatness.

Starting with I⊆H, preimage along e⁻¹ gives an ideal of K; preimage along e returns I because e⁻¹(e(h))=h. This follows the composition convention of [ideal preimage](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean#L166). Published [inverse-conjugation](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/HopfIdeal/Conjugation.lean#L108) and [identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Comap.lean#L189) controls pass. The two surjectivity witnesses come from the equivalence, not an assumption on the antipode.
Actual coordinate-conjugation inverse restores the original ideal.
Identity preimage recovers the original ideal.

The quotient projection kills exactly I, consistent with [Milne, Propositions 3.11–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78). The rendered flatness assumption on H/I supplies this particular kernel constructor’s requirements, in the sense of [Stacks, tensor exactness](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00H9). Published [surjective recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L282) and [constructor comparison](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Algebra/HopfAlgebra/HopfIdeal/Kernel.lean#L191) controls pass. The statement does not infer that every Hopf quotient is flat.
The quotient map has exactly its defining ideal as Hopf kernel, without flatness.
Surjective and flat kernel constructions agree when both are available.

The first-isomorphism equivalence has the same forward value as the canonical quotient lift, matching [Milne, Propositions 3.11–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/Books/iAG2022.pdf#page=78).
